paper_metadata.title: Impact of β-phase in TiAl alloys on mechanical properties after high temperature air exposure

evidence.quote: In this paper, the influence of high temperature air exposure on the tensile properties at room temperature and on the fatigue strength at high temperature of two TiAl alloys, is studied.
These results seem to indicate an influence of the presence of β phase on the embrittlement of TiAl alloys after exposure at 650–700 °C for 500 h.
the β -containing TNM-B1 alloy is more sensitive to embrittlement than the near- γ Ti-48-2-2 alloy

Near-γ Ti–48Al–2Cr–2Nb (Ti-48-2-2) and β-containing Ti–44Al–4Nb–1Mo-0.1B (TNM-B1) alloys have been mechanically tested in tension at room temperature and in fatigue at 633–683 °C after pre-exposure in air at high temperature (650–700 °C, 500 h).

We interpret this as a consequence of oxygen diffusion during the high temperature air exposure, which would promote formation of α 2 phase in which oxygen solubility is high, at the expenses of the β and γ phases of lower oxygen solubility.
Destabilization of the γ and β phases results then probably from oxygen diffusion.
Consequently, transformation of β into α 2 can be accounted for by an influence of oxygen.
